records.source: Καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ Σαδδουκαῖοι πειράζοντες ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν σημεῖον ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐπιδεῖξαι αὐτοῖς.
records.gloss: And having come the Pharisees and Sadducees testing asked him a sign out of the heaven to show them.
pieces: Pharisees and Sadducees came to put Jesus to the test. They asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to show them a sign from heaven.

L.1: And the Pharisees and Sadducees came, and testing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to show them a sign from heaven.

R.1: Some Pharisees and Sadducees came to Jesus. They wanted to trap {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. So they asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to show them a sign from heaven to prove that God had sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: the Pharisees and Sadducees: two rival groups acting together
decisions.reason: The Sadducees were the priestly leaders in Jerusalem and denied the resurrection (22:23); the Pharisees were teachers of the law with a strong following among the people. They differed sharply, but here both oppose Jesus, as in 3:7.

decisions.choice: testing: trying to trap him
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of the devil testing Jesus (4:1, 3). They ask for proof hoping he will fail to give it.

decisions.choice: a sign from heaven: a sign from God, plainly shown
alternatives: a sign in the sky only
decisions.reason: "Heaven" often stands for God. They want an unmistakable sign that God backs Jesus, as in 12:38.

decisions.choice: to prove that God had sent him
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sign was meant to show, as in 12:38.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new scene begins, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

records.heading: Asked for a sign from heaven

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὀψίας γενομένης λέγετε· Εὐδία, πυρράζει γὰρ ὁ οὐρανός·
records.gloss: He but answering said to them, Evening having come you say, Fair weather, is red for the sky;
pieces: He answered them, "In the evening you say, 'It will be fine weather, because the sky is red.'

L.2: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered and said to them, "When evening comes, you say, '[It will be] fair weather, for the sky is red.'

R.2: Jesus answered, "In the evening you say, 'The weather will be good tomorrow, because the sky is red.'

decisions.choice: the sayings about the sky in 16:2-3 are present, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the sayings are missing, so Jesus's answer goes straight to 16:4
decisions.reason: Some important early manuscripts, among them Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, lack the words from "When evening comes" (16:2) to the end of 16:3; most later manuscripts have them. The sayings may have been added from a saying like Luke 12:54-56, or left out by copyists in places where a red morning sky did not mean bad weather. The SBLGNT prints them. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a red sky at evening: a sign of fair weather next day
decisions.reason: People read the weather from the color of the sky. A red evening sky promised a clear day.

decisions.choice: tomorrow
decisions.reason: Readable says that the evening sky was read as a sign of the next day's weather.

records.source: καὶ πρωΐ· Σήμερον χειμών, πυρράζει γὰρ στυγνάζων ὁ οὐρανός.
records.gloss: And in the morning, Today a storm, is red for being overcast the sky.
pieces: And in the morning you say, 'There will be a storm today, because the sky is red and threatening.'

L.3: And in the morning, 'Today [there will be] a storm, for the sky is red [and] overcast.'

R.3: And in the morning you say, 'There will be a storm today, because the sky is red and dark with clouds.'

decisions.choice: present, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: See the note on 16:2. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: red and overcast: the sky is red and gloomy together
decisions.reason: The participle describes the sky as darkened with clouds while it glows red, a sign of bad weather coming.

decisions.choice: you say
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat "you say" from 16:2, which the Greek leaves understood.

records.source: τὸ μὲν πρόσωπον τοῦ οὐρανοῦ γινώσκετε διακρίνειν, τὰ δὲ σημεῖα τῶν καιρῶν οὐ δύνασθε.
records.gloss: The indeed appearance of the sky you know to discern, the but signs of the times not you are able.
pieces: You know how to read the face of the sky, but you cannot read the signs of the times.

L.3: You know how to discern the appearance of the sky, but the signs of the times you are not able [to discern].

R.3: You know how to understand what the sky is telling you. But you cannot understand the signs of what God is doing in your own time.

decisions.choice: the signs of the times: what God is doing now through Jesus
decisions.reason: Jesus's works were the signs they asked for and did not see (11:2-6; 12:28). "Times" means the appointed time God has brought.

decisions.choice: no opening word of address, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: "Hypocrites!" at the start, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts begin this sentence with "Hypocrites!" The sentence belongs to the passage that some early manuscripts lack (16:2). Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the signs of what God is doing in your own time
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the times", following the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: face of the sky
decisions.reason: The Greek word means face or appearance; Balanced keeps the picture of reading a face.

records.source: Γενεὰ πονηρὰ καὶ μοιχαλὶς σημεῖον ἐπιζητεῖ, καὶ σημεῖον οὐ δοθήσεται αὐτῇ εἰ μὴ τὸ σημεῖον Ἰωνᾶ.
records.gloss: A generation evil and adulterous a sign seeks, and a sign not will be given to it except the sign of Jonah.
pieces: An evil, unfaithful generation goes looking for a sign, but the only sign it will be given is the sign of Jonah."

L.4: An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah."

R.4: The people of today are evil and are not faithful to God. They ask for a sign. But no sign will be given to them except the sign of Jonah."

decisions.choice: the sign of Jonah: as Jesus explained it in 12:39-41
decisions.reason: Jesus repeats his earlier answer. As Jonah came back from the sea creature, the Son of Man will rise from the grave (12:40).

decisions.choice: adulterous: unfaithful to God
decisions.reason: As in 12:39, the prophets call Israel's turning from God adultery (Hosea 2:2; Jeremiah 3:8).

decisions.choice: the sign of Jonah, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the sign of Jonah the prophet, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "the prophet", as in 12:39. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the wording of 12:39 at each level
decisions.reason: Jesus gives the same answer, so it is given in the same words.

records.source: καὶ καταλιπὼν αὐτοὺς ἀπῆλθεν.
records.gloss: And having left them he went away.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left them and went away.

R.4: Then Jesus left them and went away.

decisions.choice: leaving them: leaving them behind, turning away from them
decisions.reason: The verb means to leave behind. Jesus ends the conversation.

records.source: Καὶ ἐλθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ εἰς τὸ πέραν ἐπελάθοντο ἄρτους λαβεῖν.
records.gloss: And having come the disciples to the other side forgot bread to take.
pieces: When the disciples reached the other side of the lake, they found that they had forgotten to bring any bread.

L.5: And the disciples came to the other side [and] had forgotten to take bread.

R.5: The followers went across to the other side of the lake. But they had forgotten to bring bread.

decisions.choice: had forgotten: they forgot before they set out
decisions.reason: They had failed to bring bread when they left, and found it out on the way or on arriving.

decisions.choice: the other side: across the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: Jesus had come by boat to the region of Magadan (15:39) and now crosses again.

decisions.choice: of the lake
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what they crossed.

records.heading: Watch out for their yeast

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὁρᾶτε καὶ προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων.
records.gloss: The and Jesus said to them, Watch and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
pieces: Jesus told them, "Keep your eyes open, and guard yourselves against the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees."

L.6: And Jesus said to them, "Watch out and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees."

R.6: Jesus said to them, "Be careful! Watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees."

decisions.choice: yeast: an influence that spreads through the whole
decisions.reason: A little yeast works through a whole batch of dough (13:33; 1 Corinthians 5:6). Here it is a picture of a harmful influence; 16:12 says what it is.

decisions.choice: the Pharisees and Sadducees: one article for both groups
decisions.reason: As in 16:1, the two groups are treated together.

decisions.choice: leaven (L); yeast (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word is the fermented dough kept back to raise the next batch. Literal keeps the older word "leaven"; Balanced and Readable use the everyday "yeast".

records.source: οἱ δὲ διελογίζοντο ἐν ἑαυτοῖς λέγοντες ὅτι Ἄρτους οὐκ ἐλάβομεν.
records.gloss: They but were reasoning among themselves saying that Bread not we took.
pieces: They talked it over among themselves and said, "He says that because we brought no bread."

L.7: And they were discussing among themselves, saying, "[It is] because we did not bring bread."

R.7: The followers talked about this among themselves. They said, "He is saying this because we did not bring any bread."

decisions.choice: because: the disciples explain Jesus's warning to themselves
alternatives: the word only introduces their words, "We brought no bread"
decisions.reason: The small word can introduce speech or mean "because". Either way they think Jesus is talking about the bread they forgot.

decisions.choice: He says that
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the disciples were explaining.

records.source: γνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Τί διαλογίζεσθε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς, ὀλιγόπιστοι, ὅτι ἄρτους οὐκ ἐλάβετε;
records.gloss: Having known but Jesus said, Why reason you among yourselves, little-faiths, that bread not you took?
pieces: Jesus knew what they were saying, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Why are you talking among yourselves about having no bread, you who have so little faith?

L.8: But Jesus, knowing [this], said, "Why are you discussing among yourselves, you of little faith, that you did not bring bread?

R.8: Jesus knew what they were saying. He said, "Why are you talking about having no bread? Your faith is so small!

decisions.choice: little faith: trust that gives way under pressure
decisions.reason: As in 6:30, 8:26 and 14:31, the word rebukes disciples whose faith is real but weak. They worry about bread after seeing Jesus feed thousands.

decisions.choice: Jesus knew what they were saying
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out what Jesus knew.

records.source: οὔπω νοεῖτε, οὐδὲ μνημονεύετε τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους τῶν πεντακισχιλίων καὶ πόσους κοφίνους ἐλάβετε;
records.gloss: Not yet do you understand, nor remember the five loaves of the five thousand and how many baskets you took?
pieces: Do you still not understand? Have you forgotten the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many basketfuls you gathered?

L.9: Do you not yet understand, nor remember the five loaves of the five thousand and how many baskets you took up?

R.9: Do you still not understand? Remember the five loaves of bread that fed five thousand people? Remember how many baskets of leftovers you picked up?

decisions.choice: the five loaves for the five thousand: the feeding in 14:15-21
decisions.reason: Twelve baskets of pieces were left over (14:20).

decisions.choice: baskets: the ordinary carrying baskets of 14:20
decisions.reason: Matthew uses a different word here from the one in 16:10, matching the two feeding stories (14:20; 15:37).

decisions.choice: of leftovers
decisions.reason: Readable says what filled the baskets.

records.source: οὐδὲ τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἄρτους τῶν τετρακισχιλίων καὶ πόσας σπυρίδας ἐλάβετε;
records.gloss: Nor the seven loaves of the four thousand and how many large baskets you took?
pieces: Or the seven loaves for the four thousand, and how many large basketfuls you gathered?

L.10: Nor the seven loaves of the four thousand and how many large baskets you took up?

R.10: And remember the seven loaves that fed four thousand people? Remember how many big baskets of leftovers you picked up?

decisions.choice: the seven loaves for the four thousand: the feeding in 15:32-38
decisions.reason: Seven large baskets were left over (15:37).

decisions.choice: large baskets: big hampers, as in 15:37
decisions.reason: The word is used of a basket big enough to lower a man from a wall (Acts 9:25).

decisions.choice: large baskets (L); large basketfuls (B); big baskets (R)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the difference between the two kinds of baskets.

records.source: πῶς οὐ νοεῖτε ὅτι οὐ περὶ ἄρτων εἶπον ὑμῖν;
records.gloss: How not understand you that not concerning bread I spoke to you?
pieces: How can you fail to see that I was not talking to you about bread?

L.11: How do you not understand that I did not speak to you about bread?

R.11: Why do you not understand that I was not talking about bread?

decisions.choice: how do you not understand: a rebuke in question form
decisions.reason: Jesus does not expect an answer; he wants them to see the point.

records.source: προσέχετε δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων.
records.gloss: Beware but of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
pieces: Guard yourselves, I say, against the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees."

L.11: But beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees."

R.11: Watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees!"

decisions.choice: beware: a command repeating 16:6
decisions.reason: In the SBLGNT this is a new sentence, a fresh command.

decisions.choice: I say
decisions.reason: Balanced marks the repeated warning with "I say" for the force of the Greek "but".

records.source: τότε συνῆκαν ὅτι οὐκ εἶπεν προσέχειν ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης τῶν ἄρτων ἀλλὰ ἀπὸ τῆς διδαχῆς τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων.
records.gloss: Then they understood that not he said to beware of the leaven of the breads but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
pieces: Then they realized that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was not warning them against the yeast used in bread, but against what the Pharisees and Sadducees taught.

L.12: Then they understood that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had not said to beware of the leaven of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

R.12: Then the followers understood. Jesus was not telling them to watch out for yeast in bread. He was warning them about the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

decisions.choice: the teaching: their teaching and way of reading the law
decisions.reason: Jesus has already rejected the Pharisees' traditions (15:1-14). Their teaching, and the Sadducees', kept people from seeing who he was.

decisions.choice: they understood: the disciples come to understand after Jesus explains
decisions.reason: Matthew often shows the disciples understanding once Jesus explains (13:51; 17:13).

records.source: Ἐλθὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὰ μέρη Καισαρείας τῆς Φιλίππου ἠρώτα τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ λέγων· Τίνα λέγουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι εἶναι τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου;
records.gloss: Having come then Jesus into the parts of Caesarea of Philip he was asking the disciples of him saying, Whom do say the men to be the Son of the Man?
pieces: When Jesus reached the district around Caesarea Philippi, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put a question to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples: "Who do people say that the Son of Man is?"

L.13: Now when Jesus came into the region of Caesarea Philippi, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was asking {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, saying, "Who do {{gender:people|men}} say the Son of Man is?"

R.13: Jesus went to the area near the town of Caesarea Philippi. There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, "Who do people say the Son of Man is?"

decisions.choice: Caesarea Philippi: a town in the far north, near the sources of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Herod's son Philip rebuilt the town and named it for the emperor; "Philippi" set it apart from Caesarea on the Mediterranean coast. It lay at the foot of Mount Hermon in a mostly Gentile region.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus speaks of himself
decisions.reason: Jesus uses this title for himself (8:20; 12:40), and the next question asks the disciples who he is (16:15).

decisions.choice: Who do people say the Son of Man is?, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Who do people say that I, the Son of Man, am?, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "I" (in the Greek, "me"), making plain that Jesus means himself. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means people in general, so the inclusive form is the default.

records.heading: Peter's answer at Caesarea Philippi

records.source: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Οἱ μὲν Ἰωάννην τὸν βαπτιστήν, ἄλλοι δὲ Ἠλίαν, ἕτεροι δὲ Ἰερεμίαν ἢ ἕνα τῶν προφητῶν.
records.gloss: They and said, Some indeed John the Baptist, others but Elijah, others but Jeremiah or one of the prophets.
pieces: They replied, "Some say John the Baptist; others say Elijah; still others, Jeremiah or another of the prophets."

L.14: And they said, "Some [say] John the Baptist, and others Elijah, and others Jeremiah or one of the prophets."

R.14: They answered, "Some people say {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are John the Baptist. Others say {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are Elijah. And others say {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are Jeremiah or one of the other prophets."

decisions.choice: John the Baptist: John come back to life
decisions.reason: Herod Antipas thought this (14:1-2).

decisions.choice: Elijah: the prophet God promised to send before the day of the Lord
alternatives: Elijah only as a great prophet of the past
decisions.reason: Malachi 3:23-24 (4:5-6 in most translations) promised Elijah's return. Jesus said John was that Elijah (11:14).

decisions.choice: Jeremiah: the prophet of suffering and judgment
decisions.reason: Only Matthew names Jeremiah here. Why people thought of him is not said; he too warned of the temple's fall and was rejected by his own people.

decisions.choice: say you are
decisions.reason: Readable repeats the words the Greek leaves understood.

records.source: λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ὑμεῖς δὲ τίνα με λέγετε εἶναι;
records.gloss: He says to them, You but whom me do you say to be?
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "And you, who do you say that I am?"

L.15: He says to them, "But you, who do you say that I am?"

R.15: Then Jesus asked them, "What about you? Who do you say I am?"

decisions.choice: you: emphatic, the disciples set against the crowds
decisions.reason: The pronoun stands first for emphasis: whatever others say, what do you say?

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

records.source: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ Σίμων Πέτρος εἶπεν· Σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος.
records.gloss: Answering then Simon Peter said, You are the Christ the Son of the God the living.
pieces: Simon Peter answered, "You are the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the Son of the living God."

L.16: And Simon Peter answered and said, "You are the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the Son of the living God."

R.16: Simon Peter answered, "You are the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}. You are the Son of the God who lives."

decisions.choice: the Christ: the Messiah, the anointed king God promised
decisions.reason: The word has the article: Peter names Jesus as the one Israel was waiting for. Herod's advisers spoke of the Christ in the same way (2:4).

decisions.choice: the Son of the living God: the Messiah as God's Son
alternatives: a second, separate title of lesser weight
decisions.reason: God promised to be father to David's royal son (2 Samuel 7:14; Psalm 2:7). Matthew has already shown God calling Jesus his Son (3:17), and the disciples saying so in the boat (14:33).

decisions.choice: the living God: the true God, who lives and acts
decisions.reason: The phrase sets God apart from idols that have no life (Jeremiah 10:10; Psalm 42:3).

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Where the Greek has the article, the title is written "the Christ" or "the Messiah".

decisions.choice: the God who lives
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "living" means.

records.source: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Μακάριος εἶ, Σίμων Βαριωνᾶ, ὅτι σὰρξ καὶ αἷμα οὐκ ἀπεκάλυψέν σοι ἀλλ’ ὁ πατήρ μου ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς·
records.gloss: Answering then Jesus said to him, Blessed are you, Simon Barjona, for flesh and blood not revealed to you but the Father of me who in the heavens;
pieces: Jesus said to him in reply, "You are blessed, Simon son of Jonah! No human being showed you this; it was {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father in heaven.

L.17: And Jesus answered and said to him, "Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah, for flesh and blood did not reveal [this] to you, but {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father who [is] in the heavens.

R.17: Jesus answered, "Simon son of Jonah, God has blessed you! No person showed you this. My Father in heaven showed it to you.

decisions.choice: Bar-Jonah: son of Jonah, an Aramaic way of naming a man by his father
decisions.reason: "Bar" means "son" in Aramaic. John 1:42 and 21:15 call Simon's father John; the two forms may be versions of one name, or Jonah may be another name he had.

decisions.choice: flesh and blood: a human being, as opposed to God
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of humans in their weakness (1 Corinthians 15:50; Galatians 1:16). Peter did not reach this by human insight.

decisions.choice: revealed: made known what was hidden
decisions.reason: As in 11:25-27, the Father shows who the Son is to those he chooses.

decisions.choice: blessed: favored by God, as in 5:3-11
decisions.reason: Peter is in the happy state of one God has favored.

decisions.choice: Bar-Jonah (L); son of Jonah (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Aramaic form with a hyphen; Balanced and Readable translate it.

decisions.choice: God has blessed you
decisions.reason: Readable says who gives the blessing.

records.source: κἀγὼ δέ σοι λέγω ὅτι σὺ εἶ Πέτρος, καὶ ἐπὶ ταύτῃ τῇ πέτρᾳ οἰκοδομήσω μου τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, καὶ πύλαι ᾅδου οὐ κατισχύσουσιν αὐτῆς·
records.gloss: I also now to you say that you are Peter, and on this the rock I will build of me the church, and gates of Hades not will prevail against it;
pieces: And I tell you: you are Peter, and on this rock I will build {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} church. The gates of the realm of the dead will not overpower it.

L.18: And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} church, and [the] gates of Hades will not overpower it.

R.18: And I tell you, you are Peter. (The name Peter means 'rock.') On this rock I will build {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} church. Even the gates of the place of the dead will not be strong enough to defeat it.

decisions.choice: Peter and rock: a play on words
decisions.reason: The name Peter means a stone or rock, and the word for "rock" that follows comes from the same root. In Aramaic, which Jesus spoke, both would be the same word, Kepha, the name Cephas (John 1:42). Jesus gave Simon this name (10:2).

decisions.choice: this rock: Peter himself, as the apostle who has confessed Jesus
alternatives: Peter's confession of who Jesus is
the truth revealed by the Father
decisions.reason: The play on Peter's name points most naturally to Peter, who leads the apostles in the early church (Acts 2-5; Ephesians 2:20 speaks of apostles as the foundation). Others take the rock to be the faith Peter has just confessed, or Christ himself (1 Corinthians 3:11; 1 Peter 2:4-8). Christian traditions have long differed here.

decisions.choice: church: the community of Jesus's people
decisions.reason: This is the first time the word appears in the Gospels. It meant an assembly, and the Greek Old Testament uses it for the assembly of Israel gathered before God (Deuteronomy 4:10). Jesus speaks of the people he will gather as his own.

decisions.choice: the gates of Hades will not overpower it: the power of death will not overcome the church
alternatives: the church will break through the gates of Hades
evil powers will not defeat it
decisions.reason: Gates stand for a city's strength. The Old Testament speaks of "the gates of death" and "the gates of Sheol" (Isaiah 38:10; Psalm 9:14). Death will not hold or destroy the people Jesus builds. Hades is the realm of the dead, as in 11:23.

decisions.choice: Hades (L); the realm of the dead (B); the place of the dead (R)
decisions.reason: As in 11:23. "Hell" would confuse Hades with Gehenna.

decisions.choice: (The name Peter means "rock.")
decisions.reason: Readable explains the play on words, which cannot be heard in translation. It does not say what the rock is.

decisions.choice: church
decisions.reason: "Church" is the familiar word for the community Jesus gathers; the meaning decision says it is people, not a building.

decisions.choice: will not be strong enough to defeat
decisions.reason: Readable puts the verb in plain words.

records.source: δώσω σοι τὰς κλεῖδας τῆς βασιλείας τῶν οὐρανῶν, καὶ ὃ ἐὰν δήσῃς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔσται δεδεμένον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, καὶ ὃ ἐὰν λύσῃς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔσται λελυμένον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
records.gloss: I will give to you the keys of the kingdom of the heavens, and whatever if you bind on the earth will be having been bound in the heavens, and whatever if you loose on the earth will be having been loosed in the heavens.
pieces: I will hand you the keys of the kingdom of heaven: what you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and what you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven."

L.19: I will give you the keys of the kingdom of the heavens, and whatever you bind on earth will be bound in the heavens, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in the heavens."

R.19: I will give you the keys to the kingdom of heaven. Whatever you forbid on earth will be forbidden in heaven. Whatever you allow on earth will be allowed in heaven."

decisions.choice: the keys: authority to open and shut, like a royal steward's
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 22:22 God gives the steward of David's house the key to open and shut. Peter is given authority in the kingdom; Jesus condemns the scribes for shutting it (23:13).

decisions.choice: bind and loose: forbid and permit, and so declare what God requires or forgives
alternatives: condemn and set free from sin only
decisions.reason: Jewish teachers used these words for ruling what is forbidden and what is allowed. In 18:18 the same words are given to all the disciples about a sinning member of the church; compare John 20:23 on forgiving sins.

decisions.choice: will be bound: heaven confirms what is done on earth
alternatives: will already have been bound: earth carries out what heaven has decided
decisions.reason: The verb form joins "will be" with a perfect participle. It may simply mean "will be bound", or stress that heaven has decided first.

decisions.choice: forbid; allow
decisions.reason: Readable uses the sense of the Jewish teachers' terms, following the meaning decision.

records.source: τότε διεστείλατο τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἵνα μηδενὶ εἴπωσιν ὅτι αὐτός ἐστιν ὁ χριστός.
records.gloss: Then he ordered the disciples that to no one they should say that he is the Christ.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave the disciples strict orders not to tell anyone that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

L.20: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} ordered the disciples to tell no one that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.20: Then Jesus warned {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers not to tell anyone that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

decisions.choice: tell no one: not yet, before he has taught what kind of Messiah he is
decisions.reason: Many expected a Messiah who would drive out Rome. From 16:21 Jesus teaches that the Messiah must suffer, and after his resurrection the disciples are sent to tell all nations (28:19).

decisions.choice: ordered ... the Christ, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: warned (or rebuked), the reading of some manuscripts
Jesus the Christ, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts have a stronger verb for the order, and many add the name "Jesus" before "the Christ". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus after the long speech.

records.source: Ἀπὸ τότε ἤρξατο ὁ Ἰησοῦς δεικνύειν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ὅτι δεῖ αὐτὸν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἀπελθεῖν καὶ πολλὰ παθεῖν ἀπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ ἀρχιερέων καὶ γραμματέων καὶ ἀποκτανθῆναι καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγερθῆναι.
records.gloss: From then began Jesus to show to the disciples of him that it is necessary for him to Jerusalem to go away and many things to suffer from the elders and chief priests and scribes and to be killed and on the third day to be raised.
pieces: From then on Jesus began to show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples plainly that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} must go to Jerusalem. There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would suffer much from the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would be killed, and on the third day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would be raised.

L.21: From then Jesus began to show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} must go away to Jerusalem and suffer many things from the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and on the third day be raised.

R.21: From that time Jesus began to explain to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers what must happen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He had to go to Jerusalem. There the elders, the leading priests, and the teachers of the law would make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} suffer many things. He would be killed. Then on the third day God would raise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from death.

decisions.choice: from then Jesus began: the start of a new stage of the story
decisions.reason: Matthew used the same words in 4:17 when Jesus began to preach. Now he begins to speak of his death.

decisions.choice: must: it is God's will and plan
decisions.reason: The suffering is what God has purposed and Scripture foretold (26:54).

decisions.choice: be raised: raised by God
decisions.reason: The passive verb leaves God unnamed as the one who raises Jesus, as often in the New Testament (Acts 2:24).

decisions.choice: the elders, chief priests and scribes: the groups that made up the Jewish council in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Together they formed the ruling council; they condemn Jesus in 26:57-66.

decisions.choice: the wording of 4:17 at each level
decisions.reason: The same opening words are given the same English, so readers can see the parallel.

decisions.choice: God would raise him from death
decisions.reason: Readable names God, following the meaning decision.

records.heading: Jesus speaks of his coming death

records.source: καὶ προσλαβόμενος αὐτὸν ὁ Πέτρος ἤρξατο ἐπιτιμᾶν αὐτῷ λέγων· Ἵλεώς σοι, κύριε· οὐ μὴ ἔσται σοι τοῦτο.
records.gloss: And having taken aside him Peter began to rebuke him saying, Merciful to you, Lord; never will be to you this.
pieces: Peter drew {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} aside and began to object. "God forbid it, Lord!" he said. "Nothing like this will ever happen to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!"

L.22: And Peter took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} aside and began to rebuke {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "[God be] merciful to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord! This will never happen to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

R.22: Peter took Jesus aside and began to tell {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was wrong. "No, Lord!" he said. "May God keep this from ever happening to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!"

decisions.choice: [God be] merciful to you: God forbid!
decisions.reason: The phrase was a common way of rejecting something strongly, wishing that God in mercy would spare someone from it.

decisions.choice: this will never happen: the strongest form of denial
decisions.reason: Two negatives together make the denial emphatic.

decisions.choice: rebuke: speak sharply against
decisions.reason: It is the same word used when Jesus rebukes the wind (8:26). Peter is correcting his teacher.

decisions.choice: tell him that he was wrong
decisions.reason: Readable says what rebuking means here.

records.source: ὁ δὲ στραφεὶς εἶπεν τῷ Πέτρῳ· Ὕπαγε ὀπίσω μου, Σατανᾶ· σκάνδαλον εἶ ἐμοῦ, ὅτι οὐ φρονεῖς τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ ἀλλὰ τὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
records.gloss: He but having turned said to Peter, Get behind me, Satan; a stumbling block you are of me, for not you think the things of the God but the things of the men.
pieces: Jesus turned and said to Peter, "Get behind {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, Satan! You are a stumbling block in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} way. Your mind is not on God's purposes but on human ones."

L.23: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} turned and said to Peter, "Get behind {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, Satan! You are a stumbling block to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, for you do not think the things of God but the things of {{gender:people|men}}."

R.23: Jesus turned and said to Peter, "Get behind {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, Satan! You are trying to make {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} fall. You are not thinking the way God thinks. You are thinking the way people think."

decisions.choice: Satan: Peter speaks as Satan did, tempting Jesus away from the way of suffering
decisions.reason: In 4:8-10 Satan offered Jesus the kingdoms of the world without the cross, and Jesus said, "Go away, Satan." Peter's words make the same offer.

decisions.choice: get behind me: out of my way, and back to a follower's place
decisions.reason: The words are close to 4:10, but "behind me" is the same phrase as "come after me" in 16:24. Peter is to stop blocking the way and follow.

decisions.choice: stumbling block: something that trips and makes someone fall
decisions.reason: The word means a trap or an obstacle in the path. Peter's words would lead Jesus to turn from God's will.

decisions.choice: think the things of God: have God's purposes in mind
decisions.reason: The verb means to set the mind on something. Peter judges by human standards, not God's.

decisions.choice: trying to make me fall
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general.

records.source: Τότε ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Εἴ τις θέλει ὀπίσω μου ἐλθεῖν, ἀπαρνησάσθω ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀράτω τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκολουθείτω μοι.
records.gloss: Then Jesus said to the disciples of him, If anyone wants after me to come, let him deny himself and let him take up the cross of him and let him follow me.
pieces: Then Jesus told {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Anyone who wishes to come after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} must say no to self, pick up their cross, and follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.24: Then Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "If anyone wants to come after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, let {{gender:them|him}} deny {{gender:themselves|himself}} and take up {{gender:their|his}} cross and follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.24: Then Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, "Anyone who wants to come after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} must stop putting themselves first. They must carry their cross and follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: deny oneself: give up the right to one's own life and way
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of Peter denying Jesus (26:34). To deny oneself is to say no to self as master.

decisions.choice: take up his cross: as a condemned man carried his cross to execution
decisions.reason: As in 10:38. Now that Jesus has spoken of his own death (16:21), the saying is plainer.

decisions.choice: come after me: be my disciple
decisions.reason: A disciple walked behind the teacher. "After me" is the same phrase as "behind me" in 16:23.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}; {{gender:themselves|himself}}; {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: The words apply to anyone, so the inclusive forms are the default.

decisions.choice: pick up their cross (B); carry their cross (R)
decisions.reason: The wording follows 10:38.

records.heading: Taking up the cross

records.source: ὃς γὰρ ἐὰν θέλῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ σῶσαι ἀπολέσει αὐτήν· ὃς δ’ ἂν ἀπολέσῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εὑρήσει αὐτήν.
records.gloss: Whoever for if wants the life of him to save will lose it; whoever but loses the life of him on account of me will find it.
pieces: Those who want to secure their own life will lose it, and those who lose their life for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sake will find it.

L.25: For whoever wants to save {{gender:their|his}} life will lose it; but whoever loses {{gender:their|his}} life for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sake will find it.

R.25: People who try to keep their life for themselves will lose it. But people who give up their life for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will find it.

decisions.choice: life: one's life and self, here and in the age to come
decisions.reason: As in 10:39, the saying plays on two senses: life in this world, and the true life God gives.

decisions.choice: a saying Jesus gave before in 10:39
decisions.reason: Jesus repeats the saying now that he has spoken of his own death.

decisions.choice: secure (B); try to keep (R)
decisions.reason: The wording follows 10:39.

records.source: τί γὰρ ὠφεληθήσεται ἄνθρωπος ἐὰν τὸν κόσμον ὅλον κερδήσῃ τὴν δὲ ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ζημιωθῇ;
records.gloss: What for will be profited a man if the world whole he gains the but life of him forfeits?
pieces: Suppose someone gains the whole world but forfeits their life. What good will that do them?

L.26: For what will a {{gender:person|man}} be profited if {{gender:they|he}} gains the whole world but forfeits {{gender:their|his}} life?

R.26: Suppose a person got the whole world for themselves but lost their true life. What good would the world do them then?

decisions.choice: the world: all that this life can offer, wealth and power
decisions.reason: Owning the world means having everything one could want here. Compare the offer Satan made in 4:8-9.

decisions.choice: life: the self that lives beyond death, the same word as in 16:25
decisions.reason: The word can be translated "soul" (10:28). Here it is the life that is lost or found before God.

decisions.choice: forfeit: suffer the loss of, as a penalty
decisions.reason: The verb is used of losing something as a fine or penalty.

decisions.choice: true life
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the life lost is more than the life of the body.

decisions.choice: a supposition followed by a question
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the long question in two.

records.source: ἢ τί δώσει ἄνθρωπος ἀντάλλαγμα τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ;
records.gloss: Or what will give a man as an exchange of the life of him?
pieces: Or what could anyone give to buy back their life?

L.26: Or what will a {{gender:person|man}} give in exchange for {{gender:their|his}} life?

R.26: What could anyone pay to get their life back? Nothing!

decisions.choice: in exchange: a price paid to buy back a life
decisions.reason: Psalm 49:8-9 (49:7-8 in most translations) says no one can pay God the price of a life.

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer "nothing"
decisions.reason: Nothing a person has is worth as much as their life.

decisions.choice: Nothing!
decisions.reason: Readable gives the answer the question expects.

decisions.choice: buy back
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a phrase that shows the price paid.

records.source: μέλλει γὰρ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἔρχεσθαι ἐν τῇ δόξῃ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀγγέλων αὐτοῦ, καὶ τότε ἀποδώσει ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὴν πρᾶξιν αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Is about for the Son of the Man to come in the glory of the Father of him with the angels of him, and then he will give back to each according to the deed of him.
pieces: For the Son of Man is going to come with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels in the glory of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Father, and then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will repay each person for what they have done.

L.27: For the Son of Man is about to come in the glory of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Father with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels, and then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will repay each [one] according to {{gender:their|his}} conduct.

R.27: The Son of Man will come with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will have the glory of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Father. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will pay back each person for what they have done.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man coming in glory: Daniel 7:13-14
decisions.reason: Daniel sees one like a son of man coming with the clouds and receiving glory and a kingdom. Jesus speaks of his return as judge (25:31).

decisions.choice: repay each according to his conduct: Psalm 62:13 and Proverbs 24:12
decisions.reason: The psalm (62:12 in most translations) says God repays each person by what they have done. Here the Son of Man does it.

decisions.choice: is about to: is sure to come, and soon
decisions.reason: The verb speaks of what is certain and close at hand.

decisions.choice: the glory of his Father: the Son shares the Father's glory
alternatives: a glory given only for a time
decisions.reason: The glory belongs to God, and the Son of Man comes in it. The angels are called his angels, as in 13:41.

decisions.choice: {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: The judgment applies to everyone.

decisions.choice: he will have the glory of his Father
alternatives: come in the glory of his Father
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the sentence and keeps "glory".

records.source: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι εἰσίν τινες τῶν ὧδε ἑστώτων οἵτινες οὐ μὴ γεύσωνται θανάτου ἕως ἂν ἴδωσιν τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Truly I say to you that there are some of the here standing who not not shall taste of death until they see the Son of the Man coming in the kingdom of him.
pieces: Truly I tell you, among those standing here are some who will not taste death until they have seen the Son of Man coming in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom."

L.28: Truly I tell you, there are some of those standing here who will certainly not taste death until they see the Son of Man coming in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom."

R.28: I tell you the truth, some people standing here will not die before they see the Son of Man coming as king."

decisions.choice: the Son of Man coming in his kingdom: a showing of his royal power that some hearers would see in their lifetime
alternatives: his resurrection and the gift of the Spirit
the judgment on Jerusalem in AD 70
decisions.reason: Matthew follows this saying at once with the transfiguration, where three disciples see Jesus in glory (17:1-8). Others link it to the resurrection, when Jesus says all authority has been given him (28:18), or to the fall of Jerusalem (24:34). The words do not settle which is meant.

decisions.choice: taste death: die
decisions.reason: The phrase means to experience death.

decisions.choice: will certainly not: the strongest form of denial
decisions.reason: Two negatives together make the promise emphatic.

decisions.choice: die; coming as king
alternatives: taste death; coming in his kingdom
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means and puts the kingdom in plain words.

decisions.choice: I tell you the truth (R); Truly I tell you (L, B)
decisions.reason: As in 5:18, Readable puts Jesus's solemn opening in everyday words.
